info.bio:
Silverchair fue una de las bandas australianas más aclamadas de todos los tiempos y la que ha gozado de más popularidad en las últimas tres décadas en Australia. Han tenido más álbumes en el #1 que cualquier otro artista en la historia musical de dicho país y han vendido más de seis millones de copias en todo el mundo.

Los miembros de la banda contaban con tan sólo 15 años cuando su álbum debut Frogstomp (1995) debutó en el #1 en las listas de popularidad de Australia y Nueva Zelanda

scenes.name: Grunge
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El grunge, revival del hard rock de los setenta y renacimiento musical de Seattle, fue uno de los grandes fenómenos de los noventa (casi solo en EE UU). Green River lo inauguran (Come On Down) y Pearl Jam, Soundgarden, Melvins y Mudhoney fijan sus cuatro puntos cardinales; Nirvana, con Nevermind, lo convierten en una tragaperras y en la banda sonora de la crisis nerviosa de una generación. Después, Alice In Chains (Dirt), Foo Fighters, Hammerbox, GodHeadSilo, Everclear, Stone Temple Pilots, Tool (el grupo más innovador de la segunda generación: Aenima, Lateralus), God Machine, Helmet, Quicksand, Urge Overkill, los Smashing Pumpkins (Siamese Dream, Mellon Collie), Scarce, Creed, Bush, Manic Street Preachers, Silverchair.

podcast.title: The Cable Guy Soundtrack Contribution (1996)
podcast.body: Silverchair contributed to *The Cable Guy* soundtrack in 1996, an album associated with the "creepy Jim Carrey vehicle" film. The soundtrack also featured other artists like Jerry Cantrell of Alice in Chains, Porno for Pyros, and Cracker. "Silver Chair Jerry Cantrell of Allyson Chains, Porno for Pyrrho's Cracker, and primitive radio gods ended up with a hit with standing outside a broken phone booth with money in my hand."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Bridging Rock and Metal
podcast.body: Silverchair was noted alongside Soundgarden, Nirvana, and Alice in Chains as bands that "slowly closed that big attitude gap between rock and old school metal" throughout the early and mid-90s, contributing to a more open musical landscape. "bands like Soundgarden and Silverchair Nirvana and the smashing pumpkins and Alice and Chains slowly closed that big attitude gap between rock and old school metal."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Catalog Sale
podcast.body: Silverchair is mentioned as one of the artists who have "cashed out" by selling their music catalog. "Everyone from the killers to Barry Manelow to Silver Chair to the Beach Boys to members of Allison Chains have cashed out."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Catalog Sale to Sony (2020s)
podcast.body: Silverchair sold their entire music catalog to Sony, joining hundreds of other artists in the "gold rush" for catalog acquisitions. While the exact price of the deal was kept secret, it is believed the band walked away with at least an eight-figure sum, providing them with significant financial security. "Even Silver Chair cashed in. They sold their entire catalog to Sony."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Daniel Johns's Struggles with Fame and Health
podcast.body: Daniel Johns experienced immense psychological pressure from early fame, starting at 14, leading to anorexia as a coping mechanism in hopes of being left alone. After the *Diorama* record, a diet consisting solely of fruit contributed to him developing reactive arthritis, which hindered the album's immediate touring plans. "He said that his whole eating sort of thing. He just started to stop eating. Maybe people just leave him alone."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Fan Devotion and Band Evolution
podcast.body: Silverchair's undying fan devotion is attributed in part to their young start, allowing fans to grow with them. Daniel Johns consistently sought to offer something new with each project, a diversity that some fans embraced while others, preferring their early "Frogstomp" sound, "probably laughed" and left. "Daniel's always given his fans something new on every project that he's ever done."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: International Grunge Success
podcast.body: Hailing from Australia, Silverchair was a new band that garnered a record deal because their sound resembled grunge, demonstrating the genre's international reach and influence beyond its Seattle origins. "Silver chair was from Australia."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-Grunge Example
podcast.body: Silverchair was mentioned as a Post-Grunge band, part of the wave that fused alternative rock, particularly the Grunge recipe, with mainstream aesthetics, including higher guitar tunings and direct lyrical approaches. "But let's not forget about bands like Puddle of Mud and Silverchair and Live."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Publishing Catalog Sale (N/A)
podcast.body: Silverchair is among the artists who have sold their music publishing catalogs as part of a trend since the mid-2010s. "silver chair."

xref.title: Florence Welch's First Band
xref.body: This punk group was Florence Welch's very first band. Florence played guitar and sang, while her friend Mira played drums. Their practice space was spray-painted with the name of Daniel Johns from Silverchair, a crush of Florence's at the time. "Florence's first band was a punk group called The Toxic Cockroaches."
